claims.text: The starting material is a W–Cu composite containing discrete W particles or interconnected W ligaments in a Cu matrix.
Untreated W–Cu composites are prone to phase separation and interfacial void formation during service.
(CrFeTiTa)70W30 is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
A thin, continuous (CrFeTiTa)70W30 layer can be deposited at the W–Cu interface before final consolidation.
The HEA interlayer will establish a graded, coherent interfacial structure.
The HEA interlayer will reduce W–Cu interfacial energy.
The graded interfacial structure will reduce barriers to diffusion.
The HEA interlayer will suppress or limit deleterious elemental diffusion under heat flux and irradiation.
Limiting elemental diffusion will reduce the thermodynamic drive for phase separation.
The HEA has intrinsic irradiation resistance that will stabilize the W–Cu interfacial microstructure.
Interfacial stabilization by the HEA will prevent void nucleation.
The treated composite will exhibit fewer interfacial voids and less phase separation than the untreated composite.
The treated composite will have higher and more stable thermal conductivity than the untreated composite under operational heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
(CrFeTiTa)70W30 and VFeTiTaW alloys can be prepared by mechanical alloying and sintering.
The proposed composite processing is conducted under an inert atmosphere.
The interlayered W–Cu composite is applicable under high heat flux and Ar+, He+, and D+ irradiation representative of fusion-component joints.
The working-temperature mismatch between tungsten plasma-facing material and CuCrZr cooling pipes requires a thermal-barrier interlayer.
Behavior of the proposed interlayer beyond typical fusion-interface conditions and tested fluences is not established.
The untreated control will have evident phase separation and interfacial voids under the same service conditions.

Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in thermal conductivity and reductions in void formation and phase separation relative to an identically processed untreated control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator is said to reduce barriers to diffusion, which ordinarily facilitates diffusion, while the mechanism says the same interlayer limits or suppresses elemental diffusion.
